You take the semester API you built and give it the full Horse Racing API treatment: a switchable JSON/SQL data source, SQL Server in a Docker container, and JWT login that guards every write. You build this project on your own semester API domain: Finance, Recipe, Fitness/Exercise, or the domain you chose. You do not build a horse API. You copy the pattern from the class Horse Racing API and apply it to your resource.

The full stack, end to end: your MAUI MVVM app talks to your API over HTTP; the API validates a JWT on every write (POST, PUT, DELETE) and leaves the GETs public; the repository layer stores the data in a JSON file or in the SQL Server database running in your Docker container. A switchable data source. One repository interface behind your controller, with a JSON implementation and an EF Core SQL Server implementation, picked by a setting in appsettings.json.

# GritTrack

GritTrack is a cross-platform student scheduling and GPA tracking application built with **.NET MAUI** and **C#**. It helps students organize courses and assignments, monitor academic progress, and understand how their current work affects their GPA.

> Developed for the Mobile Application Development class at MSTC.

## Features

- **Course management**
  - Add, edit, view, and remove courses.
  - Track course codes, instructors, credit hours, current letter grades, and grade points.
- **Assignment tracking**
  - Organize assignments by type, including homework, quizzes, tests, projects, readings, and other work.
  - Track due dates, completion status, points, estimated effort, and notes.
  - Identify overdue and upcoming assignments.
- **GPA calculation**
  - Calculate a current GPA from tracked courses.
  - Optionally include a starting GPA and completed credits for students who are continuing an existing academic record.
- **Course search**
  - Filter the course list as you type by course name, course code, or instructor.
- **What-if GPA simulator**
  - Pick an expected score for every ungraded assignment (sliders, or one tap to set them all to 100/90/80/70%).
  - See the projected GPA, how far it is from your current GPA, and each class's projected letter grade. See [docs/course-search-and-gpa-simulator.md](docs/course-search-and-gpa-simulator.md).
- **Form validation**
  - Bad boxes get a pink outline and their own message, plus a big error banner by the button. See [docs/validation-ux.md](docs/validation-ux.md).
- **Mid-State Hub**
  - A second tab with quick-launch cards for the MSTC sites (Blackboard, Teams, Jira, Engage, MyApps, MyMSTC).
  - Paste a syllabus schedule (`Title | MM/DD/YYYY | Points`, one per line) and import it as assignments on the course you pick. See [docs/mid-state-hub.md](docs/mid-state-hub.md).
- **Academic status indicators**
  - Classify GPA progress as `Safe`, `Watch`, or `AtRisk`.
  - Dynamically update the application accent color based on GPA status.
- **Cross-platform UI**
  - Built with .NET MAUI and XAML for shared application experiences across supported platforms.
- **Extensible architecture**
  - Uses dependency injection, page models, services, and repository interfaces.
  - Course and GPA storage can be replaced later without rewriting the UI layer.

## API Endpoints

The app's data comes from `GritTrack.Api`. Courses are the main resource. Full setup is in [GritTrack.Api/README.md](GritTrack.Api/README.md).

| Method | URL | What it does | Success | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /api/courses | List all courses. Add `?grade=B+` to only get one letter grade. | 200 | |
| GET | /api/courses/{id} | Get one course. | 200 | 404 |
| POST | /api/courses | Add a course. | 201 | 400, 401, 409 |
| PUT | /api/courses/{id} | Replace a course's fields. | 200 | 400, 401, 404, 409 |
| DELETE | /api/courses/{id} | Remove a course. | 204 | 401, 404 |
| POST | /api/auth/login | Trade the demo user name and password for a token. | 200 | 400, 401, 404 |

- 400 = a field broke a validation rule.
- 401 = the write needs a login token (only when login is turned on).
- 404 = no course with that id (or login is turned off, for the login call).
- 409 = that course code already belongs to another course.

## Technology Stack

- C#
- .NET 10
- .NET MAUI

1	# GritTrack API
2	
3	The back end for GritTrack. It stores courses in **a JSON file or SQL Server** (you pick), and
4	every create, update and delete needs a **login token** (you can turn that off for a demo).
5	The MAUI app only ever talks to this API over HTTP. It never touches SQL Server.
6	
7	## Endpoints
8	
9	| Method | URL | Does | Needs login? | Success | Failure |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| POST | /api/auth/login | Trade the demo user name and password for a token. | no | 200 | 400, 401, 404 (auth is off) |
12	| GET | /api/courses | List all courses. Optional `?grade=` filters by letter grade (e.g. `?grade=B+`). | no | 200 | |
13	| GET | /api/courses/{id} | Get one course. | no | 200 | 404 |
14	| POST | /api/courses | Add a course. | yes | 201 | 400, 401, 409 |
15	| PUT | /api/courses/{id} | Replace a course's fields. | yes | 200 | 400, 401, 404, 409 |
16	| DELETE | /api/courses/{id} | Remove a course. | yes | 204 | 401, 404 |
17	
18	- 400 = a field broke a rule. The body is a standard ProblemDetails with an `errors` list.
19	- 401 = no token, a bad token, or an expired token (or a wrong password on the login call).
20	- 409 = the course code belongs to a different course. Course codes are unique.
21	
22	### What a course has to look like
23	
24	These are checked on POST and PUT. Break one and you get a 400 with the message.
25	
26	| Field | Rule |
27	| --- | --- |
28	| `name` | Required. 100 characters max. |
29	| `courseCode` | Required. 10 characters max. Has to be unique (spaces around it and upper/lower case don't count). |
30	| `instructor` | Optional. 100 characters max. |
31	| `credits` | 0 to 6. |
32	| `currentGrade` | Required. A letter grade from A to F, like `A-`, `B+` or `F`. |
33	
34	`id`, `gradePoints` and `createdAt` are set by the server. If you send them they're ignored.
35	
36	## Settings that matter
37	
38	All in `appsettings.json` unless noted.
39	
40	| Setting | Values | What it does |
41	| --- | --- | --- |
42	| `DataSource` | `Json` or `SqlServer` | Where courses live. Picked once at startup. |
43	| `Auth:Enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true`: writes need a token. `false`: anyone can write and `/api/auth/login` answers 404. |
44	| `Auth:DemoUserName` | text (default `demo`) | The one demo account. Not a secret. |
45	| `Auth:SigningKey` | long random text | **Secret.** Signs the tokens. User Secrets only. |
46	| `Auth:DemoPassword` | text | **Secret.** The demo account's password. User Secrets only. |
47	| `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` | text | **Secret.** The SQL Server password. `.env` file (or User Secrets). |
48	
49	You can override any setting for one run with an environment variable, for example
50	`DataSource=SqlServer` or `Auth__Enabled=false`, without editing a file.
51	
52	**No secrets are ever committed.** `.env`, `Data/*.json` and `Data/*.tmp` are gitignored.
53	The signing key and demo password live in `dotnet user-secrets` on your machine only.
54	If `Auth:Enabled` is `true` and a secret is missing, the app refuses to start and tells you which one.
55	
56	## From a fresh clone to a running app
57	
58	Windows with Podman, plus the Android emulator and the troubleshooting that came up on a new machine, is in
59	[docs/run-it-end-to-end.md](../docs/run-it-end-to-end.md). The steps below are the short version.
60	
61	### 1. What you need
62	
63	- .NET 10 SDK
64	- A container engine that understands `docker compose` (Docker Desktop, or Podman with the docker CLI)
65	- Node.js, only if you want to run the Postman collection from the command line (newman)
66	- For the MAUI app: the .NET MAUI workloads (see the root README)
67	
68	### 2. The SQL Server password (`.env`)
69	
70	From the repo root (the folder with `compose.yaml`):
71	
72	```bash
73	cp .env.example .env
74	```
75	
76	Open `.env` and replace the placeholder with your own password: 8 or more characters with upper case,
77	lower case and a number. Stick to letters and numbers so it is safe inside a connection string.
78	`.env` is gitignored.
79	
80	### 3. Start SQL Server
81	
82	```bash
83	docker compose up -d
84	docker compose ps
85	```
86	
87	Wait until the container shows **healthy** (about 30 seconds the first time). The data lives in a
88	named volume (`gritrack-sql-data`), so it survives restarts. To wipe it: `docker compose down -v`.
89	
90	### 4. The login secrets (User Secrets)
91	
92	Run these from the `GritTrack.Api` folder. Use your own values. Make the signing key long (32+ characters).
93	
94	```bash
95	cd GritTrack.Api
96	dotnet user-secrets set "Auth:SigningKey" "<long random text, 32+ characters>"
97	dotnet user-secrets set "Auth:DemoPassword" "<the password you want for the demo user>"
98	```
99	
100	User Secrets are only read when `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`, which the launch profile already sets.
101	
102	### 5. Create the tables
103	
104	Nothing to do: with `DataSource` = `SqlServer` the API applies the migration when it starts (it retries for
105	about 30 seconds while SQL Server wakes up). To do it by hand instead:
106	
107	```bash
108	dotnet tool restore
109	dotnet tool run dotnet-ef database update --project GritTrack.Api
110	```
111	
112	### 6. Run the API
113	
114	```bash
115	dotnet run --project GritTrack.Api
116	```
117	
118	The first two log lines tell you the mode:
119	
120	```
121	Data source: Json
122	Auth: ON
123	```
124	
125	It listens on `https://localhost:5227` (and `http://localhost:5228`). The OpenAPI document is at `/openapi/v1.json`.
126	If your browser or newman complains about the certificate, run `dotnet dev-certs https --trust` once.
127	
128	### 7. Switch the data source
129	
130	Edit `"DataSource"` in `appsettings.json` (`"Json"` or `"SqlServer"`) and restart. Or for one run only:
131	
132	```powershell
133	$env:DataSource = "SqlServer"; dotnet run --project GritTrack.Api
134	```
135	
136	JSON mode keeps its data in `Data/courses.json` (created on first write, gitignored).
137	
138	### 8. Turn login on or off
139	
140	`"Auth": { "Enabled": true }` in `appsettings.json`, or for one run: `$env:Auth__Enabled = "false"`.
141	
142	## Postman
143	
144	Files in `postman/`:
145	
146	- `GritTrack.postman_collection.json` the requests and tests
147	- `GritTrack-AuthOn.postman_environment.json` for runs with login on
148	- `GritTrack-AuthOff.postman_environment.json` for runs with login off
149	
150	**In Postman:** import all three files, pick the environment that matches how the API is running, and run the
151	collection in the Collection Runner. For the Auth ON environment, type the demo password into the
152	`demoPassword` value (it ships empty on purpose). Every request is green in both modes, with either data source.
153	The only things that change with the switch: login (404 when auth is off) and writes without a token
154	(401 when auth is on). The collection creates its own test courses and deletes them at the end.
155	
156	**From the command line** (newman):
157	
158	```bash
159	npm install -g newman
160	newman run postman/GritTrack.postman_collection.json -e postman/GritTrack-AuthOn.postman_environment.json --env-var "demoPassword=<your demo password>" --insecure
161	newman run postman/GritTrack.postman_collection.json -e postman/GritTrack-AuthOff.postman_environment.json --insecure
162	```
163	
164	`--insecure` is only needed when your machine does not trust the ASP.NET development certificate.
165	
166	The Postman files are checked by `GritTrack.Api.Tests/Postman` (valid JSON, no undefined variables, names that match the status each script checks). If you edit them, run `dotnet test GritTrack.Api.Tests` before you commit. See [docs/testing.md](../docs/testing.md).
167	
168	## Run the MAUI app
169	
170	1. Start the API (step 6). Leave it running.
171	2. Open `GritTrack.slnx` in Visual Studio, or build from the command line:
172	
173	   ```bash
174	   dotnet build GritTrack/GritTrack.csproj -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0
175	   ```
176	
177	3. Run the app. Browsing works with no login. Try to add, edit or drop a course while signed out and the app
178	   sends you to the sign in page, then finishes the save after you sign in.
179	
180	Where the app looks for the API (`GritTrack/Services/Api/ApiSettings.cs`):
181	
182	| Where the app runs | Address it uses |
183	| --- | --- |
184	| Windows | `https://localhost:5227` |
185	| Android emulator | `https://10.0.2.2:5227` (the emulator's name for your PC) |
186	| A real phone | Change `ApiSettings` to your PC's network address |
187	
188	Debug builds accept the ASP.NET development certificate on those addresses. This follows Microsoft Learn's
189	"Connect to local web services from Android emulators and iOS simulators".
190	
191	## Troubleshooting
192	
193	| Problem | Try this |
194	| --- | --- |
195	| `Auth:Enabled is true but Auth:SigningKey is missing...` | Do step 4, and run from a Development environment (the launch profile does that). Or set `Auth:Enabled` to `false`. |
196	| `DataSource is SqlServer but MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD is not set` | Do step 2. The API looks for `.env` in the current folder and every parent folder. |
197	| `docker compose up` says `set MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD in .env` | Do step 2 first. |
198	| Container never becomes healthy | `docker compose logs sql`. The password probably breaks SQL Server's rules (too short, no number). After fixing `.env`, run `docker compose down -v` and start again. |
199	| API logs `Database not ready yet` | Normal for a few seconds. If it never goes away, check `docker compose ps` and that nothing else is using port 1433. |
200	| Login works in Postman but the app says it cannot reach the server | The API is not running, or the app is on an Android emulator and `ApiSettings` points at `localhost`. |
201	| Certificate errors | `dotnet dev-certs https --trust`, or add `--insecure` to newman. |
202	| App shows "Sign in" forever on a save | You backed out of the sign in page. Save again and sign in. |
203	| Port 5227 is taken | Change `applicationUrl` in `Properties/launchSettings.json`, `ApiPort` in `ApiSettings.cs`, and `baseUrl` in the Postman environments. |
204	
205	## Demo script
206	
207	1. **Postman, auth OFF.** Start the API with `Auth__Enabled=false`. Run the collection with the Auth OFF
208	   environment: all green. Point out that writes without a token succeed and login answers 404.
209	2. **Postman, auth ON.** Restart with auth on. Run the Auth ON environment: all green. Point out the 401s on
210	   writes without a token, then the token being saved and used.

# GritTrack API

The back end for GritTrack. It stores courses in **a JSON file or SQL Server** (you pick), and
every create, update and delete needs a **login token** (you can turn that off for a demo).
The MAUI app only ever talks to this API over HTTP. It never touches SQL Server.

## Endpoints

| Method | URL | Does | Needs login? | Success | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | /api/auth/login | Trade the demo user name and password for a token. | no | 200 | 400, 401, 404 (auth is off) |
| GET | /api/courses | List all courses. Optional `?grade=` filters by letter grade (e.g. `?grade=B+`). | no | 200 | |
| GET | /api/courses/{id} | Get one course. | no | 200 | 404 |
| POST | /api/courses | Add a course. | yes | 201 | 400, 401, 409 |
| PUT | /api/courses/{id} | Replace a course's fields. | yes | 200 | 400, 401, 404, 409 |
| DELETE | /api/courses/{id} | Remove a course. | yes | 204 | 401, 404 |

- 400 = a field broke a rule. The body is a standard ProblemDetails with an `errors` list.
- 401 = no token, a bad token, or an expired token (or a wrong password on the login call).
- 409 = the course code belongs to a different course. Course codes are unique.

### What a course has to look like

These are checked on POST and PUT. Break one and you get a 400 with the message.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Required. 100 characters max. |
| `courseCode` | Required. 10 characters max. Has to be unique (spaces around it and upper/lower case don't count). |
| `instructor` | Optional. 100 characters max. |
| `credits` | 0 to 6. |
| `currentGrade` | Required. A letter grade from A to F, like `A-`, `B+` or `F`. |

`id`, `gradePoints` and `createdAt` are set by the server. If you send them they're ignored.

## Settings that matter

All in `appsettings.json` unless noted.

| Setting | Values | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataSource` | `Json` or `SqlServer` | Where courses live. Picked once at startup. |
| `Auth:Enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true`: writes need a token. `false`: anyone can write and `/api/auth/login` answers 404. |
| `Auth:DemoUserName` | text (default `demo`) | The one demo account. Not a secret. |
| `Auth:SigningKey` | long random text | **Secret.** Signs the tokens. User Secrets only. |
| `Auth:DemoPassword` | text | **Secret.** The demo account's password. User Secrets only. |
| `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` | text | **Secret.** The SQL Server password. `.env` file (or User Secrets). |

You can override any setting for one run with an environment variable, for example
`DataSource=SqlServer` or `Auth__Enabled=false`, without editing a file.

**No secrets are ever committed.** `.env`, `Data/*.json` and `Data/*.tmp` are gitignored.
The signing key and demo password live in `dotnet user-secrets` on your machine only.
If `Auth:Enabled` is `true` and a secret is missing, the app refuses to start and tells you which one.

## From a fresh clone to a running app

Windows with Podman, plus the Android emulator and the troubleshooting that came up on a new machine, is in
[docs/run-it-end-to-end.md](../docs/run-it-end-to-end.md). The steps below are the short version.

### 1. What you need

- .NET 10 SDK
- A container engine that understands `docker compose` (Docker Desktop, or Podman with the docker CLI)
- Node.js, only if you want to run the Postman collection from the command line (newman)
- For the MAUI app: the .NET MAUI workloads (see the root README)

### 2. The SQL Server password (`.env`)

From the repo root (the folder with `compose.yaml`):

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Open `.env` and replace the placeholder with your own password: 8 or more characters with upper case,
lower case and a number. Stick to letters and numbers so it is safe inside a connection string.
`.env` is gitignored.

### 3. Start SQL Server

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
```

Wait until the container shows **healthy** (about 30 seconds the first time). The data lives in a
named volume (`gritrack-sql-data`), so it survives restarts. To wipe it: `docker compose down -v`.

### 4. The login secrets (User Secrets)

Run these from the `GritTrack.Api` folder. Use your own values. Make the signing key long (32+ characters).

```bash
cd GritTrack.Api
dotnet user-secrets set "Auth:SigningKey" "<long random text, 32+ characters>"
dotnet user-secrets set "Auth:DemoPassword" "<the password you want for the demo user>"
```

User Secrets are only read when `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`, which the launch profile already sets.

### 5. Create the tables

Nothing to do: with `DataSource` = `SqlServer` the API applies the migration when it starts (it retries for
about 30 seconds while SQL Server wakes up). To do it by hand instead:

```bash
dotnet tool restore
dotnet tool run dotnet-ef database update --project GritTrack.Api
```

### 6. Run the API

```bash
dotnet run --project GritTrack.Api
```

The first two log lines tell you the mode:

```
Data source: Json
Auth: ON
```

It listens on `https://localhost:5227` (and `http://localhost:5228`). The OpenAPI document is at `/openapi/v1.json`.
If your browser or newman complains about the certificate, run `dotnet dev-certs https --trust` once.

### 7. Switch the data source

Edit `"DataSource"` in `appsettings.json` (`"Json"` or `"SqlServer"`) and restart. Or for one run only:

```powershell
$env:DataSource = "SqlServer"; dotnet run --project GritTrack.Api
```

JSON mode keeps its data in `Data/courses.json` (created on first write, gitignored).

### 8. Turn login on or off

`"Auth": { "Enabled": true }` in `appsettings.json`, or for one run: `$env:Auth__Enabled = "false"`.

## Postman

Files in `postman/`:

- `GritTrack.postman_collection.json` the requests and tests
- `GritTrack-AuthOn.postman_environment.json` for runs with login on
- `GritTrack-AuthOff.postman_environment.json` for runs with login off

**In Postman:** import all three files, pick the environment that matches how the API is running, and run the
collection in the Collection Runner. For the Auth ON environment, type the demo password into the
`demoPassword` value (it ships empty on purpose). Every request is green in both modes, with either data source.
The only things that change with the switch: login (404 when auth is off) and writes without a token
(401 when auth is on). The collection creates its own test courses and deletes them at the end.

**From the command line** (newman):

```bash
npm install -g newman
newman run postman/GritTrack.postman_collection.json -e postman/GritTrack-AuthOn.postman_environment.json --env-var "demoPassword=<your demo password>" --insecure
newman run postman/GritTrack.postman_collection.json -e postman/GritTrack-AuthOff.postman_environment.json --insecure
```

`--insecure` is only needed when your machine does not trust the ASP.NET development certificate.

The Postman files are checked by `GritTrack.Api.Tests/Postman` (valid JSON, no undefined variables, names that match the status each script checks). If you edit them, run `dotnet test GritTrack.Api.Tests` before you commit. See [docs/testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

## Run the MAUI app

1. Start the API (step 6). Leave it running.
2. Open `GritTrack.slnx` in Visual Studio, or build from the command line:

   ```bash
   dotnet build GritTrack/GritTrack.csproj -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0
   ```

3. Run the app. Browsing works with no login. Try to add, edit or drop a course while signed out and the app
   sends you to the sign in page, then finishes the save after you sign in.

Where the app looks for the API (`GritTrack/Services/Api/ApiSettings.cs`):

| Where the app runs | Address it uses |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `https://localhost:5227` |
| Android emulator | `https://10.0.2.2:5227` (the emulator's name for your PC) |
| A real phone | Change `ApiSettings` to your PC's network address |

Debug builds accept the ASP.NET development certificate on those addresses. This follows Microsoft Learn's
"Connect to local web services from Android emulators and iOS simulators".

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Try this |
| --- | --- |
| `Auth:Enabled is true but Auth:SigningKey is missing...` | Do step 4, and run from a Development environment (the launch profile does that). Or set `Auth:Enabled` to `false`. |
| `DataSource is SqlServer but MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD is not set` | Do step 2. The API looks for `.env` in the current folder and every parent folder. |
| `docker compose up` says `set MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD in .env` | Do step 2 first. |
| Container never becomes healthy | `docker compose logs sql`. The password probably breaks SQL Server's rules (too short, no number). After fixing `.env`, run `docker compose down -v` and start again. |
| API logs `Database not ready yet` | Normal for a few seconds. If it never goes away, check `docker compose ps` and that nothing else is using port 1433. |
| Login works in Postman but the app says it cannot reach the server | The API is not running, or the app is on an Android emulator and `ApiSettings` points at `localhost`. |
| Certificate errors | `dotnet dev-certs https --trust`, or add `--insecure` to newman. |
| App shows "Sign in" forever on a save | You backed out of the sign in page. Save again and sign in. |
| Port 5227 is taken | Change `applicationUrl` in `Properties/launchSettings.json`, `ApiPort` in `ApiSettings.cs`, and `baseUrl` in the Postman environments. |

## Demo script

1. **Postman, auth OFF.** Start the API with `Auth__Enabled=false`. Run the collection with the Auth OFF
   environment: all green. Point out that writes without a token succeed and login answers 404.
2. **Postman, auth ON.** Restart with auth on. Run the Auth ON environment: all green. Point out the 401s on
   writes without a token, then the token being saved and used.
3. **Switch Json to SqlServer.** Change `DataSource` (or the env var), restart, show the startup log line
   saying `Data source: SqlServer`, run the collection again: same requests, still green.
4. **Show the container is healthy.** `docker compose ps`.
5. **Startup log lines.** Show `Data source: ...` and `Auth: ...` at the top of the console.
6. **App: browse, then write.** Open the app signed out and browse the list. Tap `+ Add`, fill the form, Save:
   the app sends you to the sign in page.
7. **Login, then create / edit / drop.** Sign in. The save finishes by itself. Edit it, then drop it. Show the
   rows in SQL Server, and the create / update / delete log lines (id and code only, never a password or token).
8. **One validation error.** Add a course with the course code left blank (or a duplicate code) and show the
   message that came back from the API.
9. **30 second bug story.** Pick one real bug you hit, say what it looked like, what the cause was, and the
   one line that fixed it. (Ideas from this project: Docker Desktop would not start because Podman held the
   docker pipe; SQL Server answered on `127.0.0.1` but not on `localhost` because `localhost` resolved to IPv6.)
